skill.name: frontend-css
skill.description: Write and maintain CSS using consistent methodology (Tailwind, BEM, CSS Modules), design tokens, framework patterns, and optimized production builds. Use this skill when writing or modifying CSS files, applying utility classes, styling components, creating design systems, defining color/spacing tokens, or working with CSS frameworks. Apply when working with .css, .scss, .sass files, Tailwind config, styled-components, CSS-in-JS, or any styling code that controls visual presentation, layout, typography, and design consistency across the application.
skill.summary: Guides CSS architecture, framework styling, design tokens, layout work, and production CSS maintenance.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The static path traversal finding is confirmed because the skill directs the agent to read a parent-directory file outside the packaged skill. No prompt injection, credential access, network access, or command execution intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced CSS standard inside the skill package or replace the link with included guidance.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 29 instructs the agent to follow ../../../agent-os/standards/frontend/css.md, which reaches outside the skill package. That external read expands filesystem scope and depends on unbundled content.

content.value_statement: Frontend styling often drifts across files, components, and frameworks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward consistent CSS methods and design tokens.
actual_capabilities: Guides CSS, SCSS, SASS, and Less file edits.
Applies Tailwind utility classes to components and markup.
Supports CSS Modules, styled-components, and CSS-in-JS patterns.
Frames design token work for colors, spacing, typography, and shadows.
Helps refactor styles toward BEM or utility-first methodology.
Covers CSS production optimization, including unused style cleanup.
limitations: It references an external parent-directory standards file that is not bundled.
It does not include executable tooling or automated CSS validation.
It cannot inspect rendered UI without project files and runtime context.
It gives methodology guidance, not a complete design system.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Styling
use_cases.description: Apply one CSS methodology across React, Vue, or similar component files.

use_cases.title: Define Design Tokens
use_cases.description: Create consistent color, spacing, typography, and shadow decisions for a UI system.

use_cases.title: Review CSS Framework Usage
use_cases.description: Check Tailwind, CSS Modules, or CSS-in-JS changes for consistency and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Style a New Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for focused styling help.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to style this component with the project CSS method. Keep spacing, typography, and colors consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to refactor these styles toward the local methodology. Preserve the visual result and explain key changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Token Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to propose design tokens for colors, spacing, typography, and shadows in this interface.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production CSS
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for review and optimization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to review this styling layer for framework conflicts, unused styles, responsive issues, and production readiness.

output_examples.input: Style a settings panel that uses Tailwind.
output_examples.output: A concise styling plan with utility choices for layout, spacing, form controls, focus states, and responsive behavior.

output_examples.input: Refactor mixed CSS classes into a consistent method.
output_examples.output: A structured refactor summary that groups selectors, token use, naming changes, and visual preservation notes.

output_examples.input: Review a CSS Modules file for maintainability.
output_examples.output: A review that identifies naming issues, duplicated values, token gaps, and framework override risks.

best_practices: Provide the existing CSS methodology before asking for changes.
Include relevant component markup with the styles being reviewed.
Ask for responsive, accessible, and production-ready styling checks.
anti_patterns: Do not mix BEM, utility-first, and CSS Modules without clear boundaries.
Do not hardcode colors or spacing when project tokens exist.
Do not request visual polish without giving UI context or constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill write CSS directly?
faq.answer: It guides an AI assistant when writing or modifying frontend styling in project files.

faq.question: Which CSS methods does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions Tailwind, BEM, CSS Modules, styled-components, CSS-in-JS, SCSS, SASS, and Less.

faq.question: Can it help with design tokens?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers colors, spacing, typography, shadows, themes, and design system configuration.

faq.question: Does it include build scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill is guidance-only and does not include scripts or executable tooling.

faq.question: Can it optimize production CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for purging unused styles and resolving framework defaults.

faq.question: What security issue was found?
faq.answer: The skill references a parent-directory standards file outside the packaged skill content.
